question: A 41-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of fatigue, cough, and a 4.5-kg (10-lb) weight loss. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. He appears emaciated. A chest x-ray shows a calcified nodule in the left lower lobe and left hilar lymphadenopathy. The physician initiates therapy for the condition and informs him that he will have to return for monthly ophthalmologic examination for the next 2 months. These examinations are most likely to evaluate the patient for an adverse effect of a drug with which of the following mechanisms of action?

options.opa: Impaired protein synthesis due to binding to 30S ribosomes
options.opb: Impaired synthesis of cell wall polysaccharides
options.opd: Impaired protein synthesis due to binding to 50S ribosomes
options.ope: Impaired production of hemozoin from heme
